title: Binghamton White-Wine Spiedie Tray
seoTitle: Binghamton White-Wine Spiedie Tray | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Spiedie chicken night—Upstate NY marinade, cube char, rolls for soaking
subtitle: Binghamton-style marinated chicken cubes, Italian roll soak, and char for ten
description: Chicken breast cubes marinate in white-wine mint-sage spiedie bath, griddle on skewers until charred and 165°F, and serve with Martin's potato rolls for soaking.

steps.title: Build spiedie marinade
steps.instruction: Whisk canola oil, vinegar, Riesling, mint, sage, rosemary, and salt. Reserve 0.5 cup for roll soaking. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Marinate chicken cubes
steps.instruction: Toss chicken in remaining marinade at least 4 hours, ideally overnight refrigerated. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat grill grates
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to medium-high, 425°F. Oil grates. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Skewer and grill
steps.instruction: Thread chicken on skewers. Grill 4 minutes per side until charred and 165°F internal. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and slide off
steps.instruction: Rest skewers 5 minutes. Slide chicken into hotel pans, cover with foil, hold at 170°F. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Prep soak rolls
steps.instruction: Split Italian rolls. Brush cut sides with reserved marinade—do not oversoak or rolls fall apart. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Warm rolls briefly
steps.instruction: Warm split rolls on grill 1 minute at 350°F cut-side down for light toast. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Platter for ten
steps.instruction: Pile chicken on platters with rolls for building. About 8 oz chicken per firefighter. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Long marinade is the spiedie secret—4 hours minimum, overnight better.
Reserve clean marinade for rolls; never use raw-chicken soak.
Char matters—pale cubes taste like plain vinegar chicken.
tonightSpread: Spiedie chicken platter with soak rolls and parsley.
leftovers: Spiedie chicken subs with extra marinade.
Chop into pasta salad with oregano.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Spiedies are a regional icon—not fajitas, not shawarma. Cubes char fast on the flat-top, slide off skewers onto platters, and hold at 170°F while rolls soak up marinade at the line.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate cubes 24 hours ideally, minimum 4 hours. Griddle medium-high 425°F. Hold chicken covered at 170°F up to 35 minutes. Rolls at room temp for soaking.
